families.note: Chunli proximal tibial replacement body (hinged, tibial part) 2#, 4#, 6#, AP and lateral, with the universal extension (Ø24 x E). Digitised by Addis Ortho from the vector drawings of Chunli's 1:1 'Tibial tray' sheets (19 Oct 2026), scaled by each sheet's own ruler (the PDFs are printed at 104.2 % of 1:1 on the page; the drawn widths match the technique's w4 58/62/67 at the ruler's scale), outline at the stroke centre. The ring is the body as drawn: insert, tray and the tapered body down to the stem junction. y = 0 is the joint line: the articular surface of the 8.5 mm insert, 4.5 mm above the tray top (Kevin, Chunli, 21 Oct 2026: insert effective height = size - 4); the sheets draw the dish bottoms 3.7-4.0 above the tray top, so the drawn insert sits up to 0.8 mm below y = 0. Below the round body a key 5 mm tall (24 wide on the AP, 15.5 on the lateral) fits the 15.75 mm notch in the top of the extension or stem; there the outline is the next part's (Ø24), so the 5 mm band is drawn Ø24 in both views and the body ends at the notch floor (the stem's origin, as the stem family). The male taper below it sits inside the next part and is not drawn. Extension E: Ø24, E mm long below the body's junction and its gap (no sheet; technique p4 and the size codes; E 40/60/80/100/120 are the trial set, 50/70/90/110 only in the code list). Lateral: anterior is on the left of Chunli's drawing, the side facing the AP view (Sami, 20 Oct 2026; the femur-seat test agrees: the hinged femur of the same size seats on the insert only with this drawing mirrored, its hinge post on the body's axis), so the ring is mirrored to put anterior at +x. LENGTH (r24, Kevin, Chunli, 21 Oct 2026, Sami's rule): joint line to the stem junction fully seated = 55 (tray top to the junction, 82 - 27, all three sizes; the sheets measure 54.6-55.0) + (8.5 - 4) = 59.5 (bodyLengthMm); each taper junction keeps a gap of about 2-2.5 mm after impaction, taken as 2.25 (junctionGapMm): one junction without an extension, two with one. reconstructionMm = 59.5 + junctions x 2.25 + E (joint line to the stem's notch floor; the outline's Ø24 band runs down to it, through the gaps, where a lateral film shows only the 15.5 mm key), and the osteotomy = reconstructionMm + the stem's collar c. Chunli's technique p11 'Tibial part is the height of 70mm' is superseded. Sizes 8# and 10#: no sheet, not needed (Sami).

families.note: Chunli universal cemented stem (tumour system), round (AP and lateral the same). Parametric from the printed dimensions, checked against the sheet: proximal shaft diameter a (11/12/13), tip diameter b (8/9/10) and length (105-145 mm, from the collar's shoulder to the shaft's flat end) from the technique p4 table and Chunli's size codes; the Ø24 collar, its 5 mm top notch, the shoulder fillet and the rounded tip cap (12 mm long, wider than the tip: probably a distal centraliser; material not stated, so it is kept in the outline as the canal room it needs) measured on the drawn stem of the same diameter. c (30/40/50/60) is the collar length from the floor of its top notch to the shoulder, as drawn (solid collar 30, dashed steps 40/50/60). Origin (the junction with the extension or body) = the notch floor, so the shoulder that sits on the osteotomy is at c, as Chunli's rule osteotomy = 70 + E + c requires; the drawn 5 mm above the notch floor is taken to overlap the part above and is left out of the ring (both Ø24). The sheet draws only the longest length of each diameter in full and marks the shorter ones with lines; the shorter stems are modelled with the same taper from a to the printed b over their own length (the table gives one b per diameter). Only the 36 combinations in Chunli's size-code list are offered. nominalLengthMm = the catalogue length; drawnLengthMm = junction to the tip of the cap. Not yet confirmed by Chunli.

families.source: Chunli 1:1 vector template sheets 'Femur Tumor Prosthesis - Femur Part' #2/#4/#6 L and R (printed at 91.7 % of 1:1 on the page, scaled by their own rulers), Addis Ortho Drive COMPANIES/CN Chunli/Template/Tumor/Distal Femur Tumor/ (each pinned by SHA-256 in extract_chunli_tumour.py); 'Knee Tumor Prosthesis Surgical Technique' p17
families.note: Chunli distal femoral replacement, femoral part (hinged, with the hinge post that enters the tibial part), sizes 2#, 4#, 6#, AP and lateral. Digitised by Addis Ortho from the vector drawings of Chunli's 1:1 sheets, scaled by each sheet's ruler (the PDFs are printed at 91.7 % of 1:1 on the page; at the ruler's scale the AP widths are the manual's w3 56/61/66). The sheets draw the part distal end up: the page turns them 180 degrees. y = 0 is the joint line: the distal condyle surface (AP; the lateral takes the AP's level). The ring is the part as drawn with the hinge post, the male taper at the junction left out (it sits in the next part). LENGTH (Sami, 21 Oct 2026: the tibial logic, the same gap): joint line to the junction along the taper axis as drawn on the AP (bodyLengthMm: 2# 70.35, 4# 70.28, 6# 72.32; the manual's single figure is 70; the laterals draw the junction 1.0-1.7 mm further, gated at 2, recorded; the page warns where a size differs from the manual by more than 1 mm: 6#); each taper junction about 2-2.5 mm open, 2.25 used (one without an extension, two with one); reconstructionMm = body + junctions x 2.25 + E, the osteotomy above the joint line = reconstructionMm + the stem's collar c. The Ø24 band (second ring) runs from the junction through the gaps and the extension to the stem's notch floor. The taper leans 5 degrees on the AP: each side takes the drawing that leans the way a femoral canal does on a standard AP film (the sheet labelled L fits a right knee, as on the proximal tibial femur sheets). Lateral: anterior +x (left as drawn, the side facing the AP view; Sami). 8#/10#: sheets without a ruler, not offered. Not yet confirmed by Chunli.
